items.plain: Our salvation rests on hope, and hope is for what we cannot yet see. If we already saw it, we would not need to hope; since we don't, we wait for it patiently.
items.core_idea: Hope is for the unseen, so we wait patiently

items.plain: For those who love God and are called by his purpose, everything that happens works together for good.
items.core_idea: For those who love God, all works for good

items.plain: Paul is certain that nothing at all, not death or life, angels or powers, present or future, high or low, or anything created, can cut us off from God's love in Christ Jesus.
items.core_idea: Nothing can separate us from God's love in Christ

items.plain: Don't shape yourself to fit this world; let your mind be renewed and changed, so you can discover and live out God's good, pleasing and perfect will.
items.core_idea: A renewed mind, not conformity, reveals God's will

items.plain: Love sincerely, without pretence. Hate what is evil and hold tight to what is good.
items.core_idea: Love sincerely, hate evil, hold to good

items.plain: Bless people who mistreat you instead of cursing them. Share others' joy and grief, live in harmony, spend time with humble people rather than chasing status, and don't think yourself wise.
items.core_idea: Bless enemies, share feelings, stay humble

items.plain: Don't pay back wrong with wrong or take revenge; leave that to God. Live at peace with everyone as far as you can, feed your hungry enemy, and defeat evil by doing good.
items.core_idea: Overcome evil with good, not revenge

items.plain: The only debt you should carry is the duty to love each other. All the commandments come down to loving your neighbour as yourself, because love never harms anyone, and so love fulfils the law.
items.core_idea: Love of neighbour fulfils the whole law

items.plain: The night is nearly over and day is coming, so let's drop the deeds of darkness and put on light like armour.
items.core_idea: Day is near; leave darkness, wear light

items.plain: None of us lives or dies only for ourselves. Whether we live or die, we do it for the Lord, and we belong to him.
items.core_idea: In life and death we belong to the Lord

items.plain: Those of us who are strong should carry the weaknesses of the weak rather than pleasing ourselves. Each of us should please our neighbour in ways that do them good and build them up.
items.core_idea: The strong should carry the weak

items.plain: A prayer that the God of hope will fill you with joy and peace as you trust him, so that the Holy Spirit's power makes your hope overflow.
items.core_idea: May God fill you with joy, peace, hope

items.plain: Ruth begs Naomi not to send her away: wherever Naomi goes or lives, Ruth will too; Naomi's people and God will be hers, and only death will part them.
items.core_idea: Loyal love that refuses to leave

items.plain: Naomi tells the townspeople not to call her Naomi, meaning pleasant, but Mara, meaning bitter: she left full and God has brought her home empty and afflicted.
items.core_idea: Grief renames you: I left full, came back empty

items.plain: Unjust anger can never be excused; it brings a man down. A patient man holds on for a while, and joy comes to him later; he keeps quiet for a time, and many will praise his wisdom.
items.core_idea: Patience outlasts anger and brings joy later

items.plain: If you set out to serve the Lord, expect to be tested. Hold steady, don't panic in disaster, stay close to him and accept hardship patiently; gold is proved in fire, people in humiliation. Trust him and hope in him.
items.core_idea: Serving God means enduring testing with trust

items.plain: Look back through history: who ever trusted the Lord and was let down, stayed faithful and was abandoned, or called on him and was ignored? The Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives and rescues in trouble.
items.core_idea: No one who trusted the Lord was abandoned

items.plain: Look after your father in his old age and don't cause him grief. Be patient if his mind fails, and don't look down on him while you are strong; caring for him will be remembered and will build you up.
items.core_idea: Care patiently for your ageing father

items.plain: Do your work humbly and good people will love you. The greater you become, the more you should humble yourself, and you will find favour with the Lord.
items.core_idea: The greater you are, the humbler be

items.plain: Don't chase things too hard or beyond your strength. Think about what you have been told to do; you don't need hidden things. Don't fuss over unnecessary matters, since you've been shown more than people can grasp.
items.core_idea: Attend to what's given, not what's beyond you

items.plain: Don't take away a poor person's living or keep the needy waiting. Don't add sorrow to the hungry or trouble to someone already distressed; give promptly, and don't turn away from a poor person who asks.
items.core_idea: Don't turn away from the poor and needy

items.plain: Watch for the right moment, avoid evil, and don't be ashamed to stand up for yourself. Some shame leads to sin, and some shame is honourable and gracious.
items.core_idea: There is a bad shame and a good shame

items.plain: Be quick to listen and slow to answer. If you understand, reply; if not, keep your hand over your mouth. Talk brings honour or disgrace, and a person's tongue can be their downfall.
items.core_idea: Listen quickly, answer slowly; the tongue can ruin you

items.plain: Test a friend before trusting them. Some friends stay only while it suits them, some turn hostile and expose your quarrels, and some share your table and good times but turn against you when you fall.
items.core_idea: Test friends; many vanish when trouble comes

items.plain: A faithful friend is strong protection and a real treasure; nothing can be traded for one, and their worth is beyond price. A faithful friend is like life-giving medicine, and those who fear the Lord will find one.
items.core_idea: A faithful friend is a priceless treasure

items.plain: Seek instruction from youth onward, and you will still be finding wisdom when your hair is grey. Approach wisdom like a farmer who ploughs, sows and waits; the work is small and you will soon enjoy the harvest.
items.core_idea: Cultivate wisdom early like a patient farmer

items.plain: Don't mock someone when they are in bitter pain, because there is One who brings people low and lifts them up.
items.core_idea: Never mock someone in their bitterness

items.plain: Honour your father wholeheartedly and don't forget your mother's labour pains. Remember they gave you life: how could you ever repay what they have done for you?
items.core_idea: Honour parents; you can never repay them

items.plain: Don't fail those who weep; mourn with those who mourn. Be quick to visit the sick, for this wins love. In everything, remember your death, and you will never go wrong.
items.core_idea: Comfort mourners, visit the sick, remember death

items.plain: Don't shame someone who turns away from sin, since we all deserve punishment. Don't dishonour the old, since we are ageing too. Don't gloat over the dead; remember that we all die.
items.core_idea: Don't scorn others; we share their fate

items.plain: Don't abandon an old friend, because a new one doesn't compare. A new friend is like new wine: once it has aged, you will enjoy it.
items.core_idea: Old friends, like aged wine, are best

items.plain: Don't envy the success of a wrongdoer; you don't know how he will fall.
items.core_idea: Don't envy the wicked's success

items.plain: Don't be angry with your neighbour over every wrong, and never act through violence.
items.core_idea: Don't rage over every wrong

items.plain: Respect yourself humbly and give yourself the honour you deserve. Who will defend someone who sins against their own soul, or honour someone who disrespects their own life?
items.core_idea: Humbly honour your own soul

items.plain: Don't praise someone for their looks or despise them for their appearance. The bee is small among flying creatures, yet what it makes is the sweetest of all.
items.core_idea: Don't judge by appearances; the small bee makes honey

items.plain: Many kings have ended up sitting on the ground, while someone no one noticed has worn a crown. Many powerful men have been disgraced, and famous ones handed over to others.
items.core_idea: Fortune topples the great and raises the unknown

items.plain: Don't blame before you've looked into it; understand first, then correct. Don't answer before you've listened, and don't interrupt someone mid-speech.
items.core_idea: Understand and listen before you judge or answer

items.plain: Don't busy yourself with too many things: meddling brings trouble, and chasing or fleeing gets you nowhere. Some people toil, labour and rush, and fall further behind for it.
items.core_idea: Too much busyness leaves you further behind

fix.display_text: My son, be not busy about many matters: For if you meddle much, you will not be unpunished; And if you pursue, you will not overtake; And you will not escape by fleeing. There is one that toileth, and labors, and makes haste, And is so much the more behind.

items.plain: Some grow rich by scrimping and caution, and say, now I can rest and enjoy my goods. But he doesn't know how long he has; he will die and leave it all to others.
items.core_idea: Hoarded wealth is left to others at death

items.plain: In good times we forget the bad, and in bad times the good. The Lord can easily repay someone at death; an hour of pain erases pleasure, and a person's end reveals their deeds.
items.core_idea: A person's end reveals the truth of their life

items.plain: You can't really test a friend when things are going well, and an enemy can't stay hidden when things go badly. When you prosper your enemies are upset; when you struggle even a friend will pull away.
items.core_idea: Hard times reveal true friends and enemies

items.plain: When a rich man stumbles, friends hold him up and excuse his words; when a poor man falls, they push him away and ignore his wisdom. People praise the rich and ask of the poor, who is this?
items.core_idea: The world props up the rich and shuns the poor

items.plain: Happy is the person who hasn't slipped up in speech and isn't stung by regret for sins. Happy is the one whose own soul doesn't condemn them and who hasn't lost hope.
items.core_idea: Blessed is a clear conscience that keeps hope

items.plain: Treat yourself well with what you have, and give to the Lord properly. Death won't wait, so be generous to your friend while you live, and don't let a good day pass you by.
items.core_idea: Death won't wait; enjoy and give now

items.plain: All living things wear out like clothing; the oldest rule is that we die. Like leaves on a tree, some fall and some grow, so generations end and others are born. Every work decays, and its maker departs with it.
items.core_idea: Generations fall and grow like leaves

items.plain: God made humans from the start and left them free to choose. You can keep the commandments if you want to; fire and water, life and death are set before you, and whichever you reach for will be yours.
items.core_idea: God gave us free choice between life and death

items.plain: Don't tell yourself you can hide from the Lord, that no one up there will remember you, that you'll be lost among so many people, or that your soul counts for nothing in a boundless creation.
items.core_idea: Don't think you're too small for God to notice

items.plain: When a person thinks they've finished, they are only beginning. What is a human, and what is their good or evil? A hundred years at most: a drop from the sea against eternity.
items.core_idea: A lifetime is a drop against eternity

items.plain: A person's mercy reaches their neighbour, but the Lord's mercy reaches every living being; he corrects, disciplines and teaches, and brings people back like a shepherd with his flock.
items.core_idea: God's mercy shepherds everyone

items.plain: Don't spoil your good deeds or hurt people with words when you give. As dew cools scorching heat, a kind word is worth more than a gift, and a gracious person offers both.
items.core_idea: A kind word is better than a gift

items.plain: When you have plenty, remember hunger; when you are wealthy, remember poverty and need. Things change between morning and evening, and everything passes quickly before the Lord.
items.core_idea: In plenty, remember want; things change fast

items.plain: Have you heard something said? Let it die with you. Take heart: keeping it won't make you burst.
items.core_idea: Keep what you hear to yourself

items.plain: If you hear something against a friend, ask them: perhaps they didn't do or say it, and if they did, they may stop. Slander is common, so don't believe every word; who has never slipped with their tongue?
items.core_idea: Ask a friend before believing what you hear

items.plain: Some keep silent and are thought wise; others are disliked for talking too much. Some are silent for lack of an answer, others because they know their moment. The wise wait; the boaster and fool don't.
items.core_idea: The wise keep silent until the right time

items.plain: Some people find good fortune in misfortune, and some gains turn into losses. Some gifts bring no benefit, others pay back double. Some are brought low by glory, and some rise from a low place.
items.core_idea: Fortune and misfortune often reverse

items.plain: Have you sinned? Don't add more to it, and pray to be forgiven for what you've already done.
items.core_idea: After sinning, stop and seek forgiveness

items.plain: When a thoughtful person hears a wise saying, they praise it and build on it. When a careless person hears it, they dislike it and toss it behind their back.
items.core_idea: The wise welcome wisdom; the careless discard it

items.plain: Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the wise keep their mouth in their heart.
items.core_idea: Fools blurt; the wise speak from the heart

items.plain: Weep for the dead, who have lost the light, and weep for a fool, who has lost understanding. Weep more gently for the dead, because they are at rest; a fool's life is worse than death.
items.core_idea: A fool's life is worse than death

items.plain: Timber bound into a building won't shake loose, and a heart settled on sound advice won't be afraid. But stakes on a hilltop fall in the wind, and a fool's fearful heart gives way to any fear.
items.core_idea: A heart grounded in good counsel stands firm

items.plain: Taunting a friend ends a friendship. Even after a drawn sword or harsh words there can be reconciliation, but not after insult, arrogance, a betrayed secret or a treacherous blow; those drive any friend away.
items.core_idea: Friendship survives anger, not betrayal

items.plain: Earn your neighbour's trust while they are poor, so you can share their gladness when they prosper. Stand by them in hard times, so you can share in their good fortune.
items.core_idea: Stand by people in hard times

items.plain: The speaker wishes someone would guard his mouth and seal his lips with good sense, so that he doesn't slip and his own tongue doesn't destroy him.
items.core_idea: A prayer to guard one's tongue

items.plain: The speaker names three things that made her beautiful before God and people: relatives who get along, neighbours who are friends, and a wife and husband who live in harmony.
items.core_idea: Harmony in family, neighbours and marriage is beautiful

items.plain: If you gathered nothing when young, how will you have anything when old? Good judgement and counsel are beautiful in the grey-haired. Long experience is the crown of the old, and their pride is the fear of the Lord.
items.core_idea: Experience is the crown of old age

items.plain: Rich or poor, a good heart always brings a cheerful face.
items.core_idea: A good heart gives a cheerful face

items.plain: The speaker was afraid of three things, and prayed about a fourth: a whole city's slander, a mob gathering, and a false accusation. All of these are worse than death.
items.core_idea: Slander and false accusation are worse than death

items.plain: A kiln tests a potter's pots, and a person is tested by how they reason. As fruit shows how a tree was tended, words show the heart. Don't praise anyone before you hear them reason.
items.core_idea: Words reveal the heart; judge by reasoning

items.plain: Love a friend and keep faith. If you reveal their secrets, don't chase them; the friendship is gone like a bird let loose. A wound can heal and insults be forgiven, but betraying secrets leaves no hope.
items.core_idea: Betraying a secret destroys a friendship for good

items.plain: Forgive your neighbour and your sins will be forgiven when you pray. How can someone nurse anger yet ask the Lord for healing, or refuse mercy yet beg it? Remember death, drop hostility, overlook others' faults.
items.core_idea: Forgive others to be forgiven yourself

items.plain: A quarrel started in haste lights a fire, and a hasty fight sheds blood. Blow on a spark and it burns; spit on it and it goes out, and both come from the same mouth.
items.core_idea: Your mouth can fan or quench a quarrel

items.plain: A whip leaves a mark on the skin, but a tongue's blow breaks bones. Many have died by the sword, but not as many as have fallen because of the tongue.
items.core_idea: The tongue wounds more than the sword

items.plain: What life really needs is water, bread, clothing and a roof. A poor man's life under a log shelter is better than lavish food in someone else's house. Whether you have little or much, be content.
items.core_idea: Be content with little or much

items.plain: A poor man who is healthy is better off than a rich man plagued by illness. Health is worth more than all gold; no wealth beats a healthy body, and no gladness beats joy of heart.
items.core_idea: Health is worth more than wealth

items.plain: Don't give yourself over to sorrow or torment yourself with your thoughts. Gladness of heart is life and lengthens your days. Comfort your heart and push sorrow away; envy, anger and worry age you early.
items.core_idea: Don't give yourself to sorrow; gladness is life

items.plain: Lying awake over wealth wears down the body, and its worries drive away sleep. Anxious wakefulness longs for sleep, and serious illness breaks it.
items.core_idea: Worry over money steals sleep

items.plain: Wine drunk in moderation is as good as life; it was made to gladden people. Taken at the right time and amount it brings joy, but drunk heavily it brings bitterness and fighting.
items.core_idea: Wine in measure gladdens; in excess embitters

items.plain: Young man, speak if you are needed, but hardly at all unless asked twice. Keep it short, say much in few words, and be like someone who knows but holds their tongue.
items.core_idea: Speak little; say much in few words

items.plain: Do nothing without taking advice, and once you have acted, don't regret it.
items.core_idea: Seek advice first, then don't regret

items.plain: Empty and false hopes belong to a person without sense, and dreams lift fools off the ground. Fixing your mind on dreams is like grabbing at a shadow or chasing the wind.
items.core_idea: Chasing dreams is grasping at shadows

items.plain: A well-taught, experienced person understands much; the inexperienced know little, but travel builds skill. The speaker has seen much in his wanderings, understands more than he can say, and survived deadly dangers because of it.
items.core_idea: Experience and travel deepen understanding

items.plain: Everyone says they are your friend, but some friends are friends only in name. Isn't it a grief close to death when a companion and friend turns into an enemy?
items.core_idea: A friend turned enemy is a deathly grief

items.plain: Don't forget a friend in your heart, and don't neglect them when you become rich.
items.core_idea: Don't forget friends when you prosper

items.plain: Hold firm to what your own heart advises, because nothing is more faithful to you. A person's soul can sometimes tell them more than seven watchmen sitting high on a tower.
items.core_idea: Trust the counsel of your own heart

items.plain: Let reasoning begin every task, and let advice come before every action.
items.core_idea: Think and take advice before acting

items.plain: Test your soul throughout your life, notice what is bad for it, and don't give it that. Not everything is good for everyone, and not everyone enjoys the same things.
items.core_idea: Learn what harms you and avoid it

items.plain: Let your tears fall for the dead and lament deeply; prepare the body and don't neglect the burial. Mourn bitterly as the person deserves, for a day or two, and then be comforted in your sorrow.
items.core_idea: Mourn fully, then let yourself be comforted

items.plain: Don't give your heart to sorrow; remember your own end. The dead won't return, and grief harms you without helping them. Their fate will be yours: yesterday me, today you. Let their memory rest, and be comforted.
items.core_idea: Don't drown in grief; the dead are at rest

fix.display_text: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself. Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall yours be; Yesterday for me, and today for you. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.

items.plain: People live with anger, jealousy, trouble, fear of death and strife. Even in bed their rest is short; in sleep they are troubled as if fleeing a battle, then wake amazed the fear was nothing.
items.core_idea: Anxiety haunts even our sleep, then proves empty

items.plain: The life of someone who works and is content will be sweet, but finding a treasure is better than both.
items.core_idea: Contented work makes life sweet

fix.display_text: The life of one that labors, and is contented, shall be made sweet; And he that finds a treasure is above both.

items.plain: Wine and music gladden the heart, but the love of wisdom is better than both.
items.core_idea: Love of wisdom beats wine and music

items.plain: Don't fear the sentence of death; it is the Lord's decree for everyone before and after you, so why resist it? Whether you live ten, a hundred or a thousand years, the grave doesn't ask.
items.core_idea: Death comes to all; don't fear it

items.plain: Take care of your reputation; it stays with you longer than a thousand fortunes in gold. A good life lasts a limited number of days, but a good name lasts forever.
items.core_idea: A good name outlasts life and gold

items.plain: Keep what you have been taught, but hidden wisdom and buried treasure are of no use to anyone. Better someone who hides their foolishness than someone who hides their wisdom.
items.core_idea: Hidden wisdom is useless; share it

items.plain: A mist that comes quickly heals everything, and dew that falls after the heat brings cheer.
items.core_idea: Relief after heat brings healing and cheer

items.plain: We can say many things and still fall short; the sum of all our words is that he, God, is everything.
items.core_idea: Words fall short; God is all

items.plain: The speaker was near death, surrounded, with no one to help and no human aid coming. Then he remembered the Lord's mercy and his age-old works, how he rescues those who wait for him.
items.core_idea: With no help left, remember God's mercy

items.plain: While still young, the speaker openly sought wisdom in prayer before the temple and will seek her to the end. He delighted in her, followed her uprightly from youth, listened a little and learned much.
items.core_idea: Seek wisdom from youth to the end

items.plain: Do your work before the time comes, and in his own time God will reward you.
items.core_idea: Do your work; reward comes in God's time

items.plain: The speaker begs the women of Jerusalem, by the deer of the field, not to stir up or awaken love until love itself is ready.
items.core_idea: Don't awaken love before its time

items.plain: Her beloved calls her to rise and come away with him: winter and rain are over, flowers are out, birds are singing, figs are ripening and the vines are in fragrant blossom.
items.core_idea: Winter is past; love calls you to come away

items.plain: At night in bed she looked for the one she loves and couldn't find him. She resolves to get up and search the city's streets and squares for him, but still she doesn't find him.
items.core_idea: Searching for a loved one and not finding

items.plain: I belong to the one I love, and the one I love belongs to me.
items.core_idea: Lovers belong wholly to each other

items.plain: Keep me as a seal on your heart and arm, for love is as strong as death, its passion a blazing flame of God. No flood can drown love, and anyone trying to buy it with wealth would be scorned.
items.core_idea: Love is strong as death and can't be bought

items.plain: A prayer to God: we follow you wholeheartedly, revere you and seek your face. Don't let us be shamed, but treat us with your kindness and your great mercy.
items.core_idea: We follow you; deal with us in mercy

items.plain: Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good and his mercy lasts forever.
items.core_idea: Give thanks; God's mercy lasts forever

items.plain: To people who are pure, everything is pure; but to those who are corrupted and don't believe, nothing is pure, because their very minds and consciences are corrupted.
items.core_idea: To the pure, all things are pure

items.plain: Tobit tells his child not to look down on their mother but to honour and please her and not grieve her all her life, remembering the dangers she went through for them while pregnant.
items.core_idea: Honour your mother all her days

items.plain: Give to the poor from what you own, without begrudging it, and God won't turn from you. Give much if you have much, and a little without fear if you have little; giving protects from death and darkness.
items.core_idea: Give to the poor from whatever you have

items.plain: Don't do to anyone what you yourself hate.
items.core_idea: Don't do to others what you hate

items.plain: Ask advice from every wise person, and don't scorn any useful counsel.
items.core_idea: Seek advice from the wise

items.plain: Tobit tells his child not to fear because they have become poor: you have great wealth if you revere God, turn away from all sin and do what pleases him.
items.core_idea: Fearing God is true wealth, even in poverty

items.plain: Don't be greedy to pile up money; let it be rubbish compared to our child. What the Lord has given us to live on is enough.
items.core_idea: What God gives is enough; people matter more

items.plain: Do good and evil won't find you. Prayer with fasting, giving and righteousness are good. A little gained honestly is better than much gained wrongly, and giving to the poor is better than hoarding gold.
items.core_idea: A little with goodness beats much without

items.plain: Beware of pointless grumbling and keep your tongue from backbiting, because no secret word goes without effect, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.
items.core_idea: Grumbling and lies harm your own soul

items.plain: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand and no torment will touch them. To foolish eyes they seemed to die, and their leaving looked like disaster and ruin, but they are at peace.
items.core_idea: The righteous dead are at peace in God's hand

items.plain: A righteous person who dies young will be at rest. Honourable old age isn't measured by length of time or number of years; understanding is a person's grey hair, and a blameless life is ripe old age.
items.core_idea: A good life, not long years, is true old age

items.plain: Wisdom is radiant and never fades; those who love and seek her find her easily, as she shows herself first. Whoever rises early finds her at the door; thinking of her frees you from worry.
items.core_idea: Wisdom is easily found by those who seek her

items.plain: The king says he is mortal like everyone: formed in a womb, born breathing the same air, giving the same first cry, nursed with care. No king begins differently; all enter and leave life alike.
items.core_idea: Kings and all people share one birth and death

items.plain: Who can know God's plan or will? Human thoughts are timid and our plans fail; the body weighs down the soul and the worried mind. We barely grasp earthly things, so who has traced heavenly ones?
items.core_idea: Human minds can't fathom God's plan

items.plain: A prayer to God: you love everything that exists and hate nothing you made, or you wouldn't have made it. You spare all things because they are yours, Lord who loves life; your spirit is in everything.
items.core_idea: God loves everything he made; his spirit is in all

fix.display_text: For you love all things that are, And abhor none of the things which you did make; For never would you have formed anything if you did hate it. And how would anything have endured, except you had willed it? Or that which was not called by you, how would it have been preserved? But you spare all things, because they are yours, O Sovereign Lord, you lover of men’s lives; For your incorruptible spirit is in all things.

items.plain: Wickedness, condemned by its own conscience, is cowardly and always expects the worst. Fear is simply giving up the help reason offers, and the less help we expect within, the more frightening the unknown becomes.
items.core_idea: Fear is abandoning the help of reason

items.plain: God's message to Zerubbabel: it will be done not by strength or power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of Armies.
items.core_idea: Not by might or power, but by God's Spirit

items.plain: Who would look down on a day of small beginnings?
items.core_idea: Don't despise small beginnings

items.plain: Judge fairly and show kindness and compassion to one another. Don't oppress widows, orphans, foreigners or the poor, and don't secretly plot harm against each other.
items.core_idea: Be just and kind; don't oppress the vulnerable

fix.display_text: Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother. Don’t oppress the widow, nor the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.
fix.reason: Unmatched closing quotation mark at end

items.plain: God says: this is what you must do. Tell each other the truth, judge truly and make peace in your courts, don't plot harm against your neighbour, and don't love false oaths, for I hate all these things.
items.core_idea: Speak truth, judge fairly, plot no harm

fix.display_text: These are the things that you shall do: speak every man the truth with his neighbor. Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates, and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor, and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, says Yahweh.

items.plain: Come back to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope! God declares that even today he will give you back double.
items.core_idea: Prisoners of hope will be restored double

items.plain: The Lord your God is with you, a mighty saviour. He delights in you with joy, quiets you with his love, and rejoices over you with singing.
items.core_idea: God rejoices over you with singing

items.plain: A small bird nesting in a huge forest uses only one twig, and a tapir drinking from a river takes only enough to fill its belly.
items.core_idea: Take only what you need

items.plain: If you have a big tree and don't know its use, plant it in the realm of nothingness and rest idly in its shade. No axe will touch it, because being useless to others keeps it safe from harm.
items.core_idea: Being useless to others can keep you safe

items.plain: Joy, anger, sorrow, happiness, caution and regret take turns in us, rising like music from hollows or mushrooms from damp. Day and night they change, and we can't tell where they come from, let alone their cause.
items.core_idea: Moods rise in us from unknown sources

items.plain: Isn't it pitiful to be worn down by life and rush through it unable to stop? Isn't it a real grief to toil endlessly, never enjoy the results, and then leave, exhausted, for who knows where?
items.core_idea: Endless toil without enjoying life is pitiful

items.plain: The perfect Tao doesn't announce itself. Perfect argument isn't put into words, perfect kindness doesn't show itself in deeds, perfect honesty isn't rigidly incorruptible, and perfect courage isn't rigidly unyielding.
items.core_idea: The highest things don't show themselves

items.plain: You're going too fast: you see an egg and expect to hear it crow, you look at your crossbow and expect roast duck already in front of you.
items.core_idea: Don't expect results before they can come

items.plain: How can I know that loving life isn't a delusion? How can I know that someone who dreads death isn't like a lost child who can't find the way home?
items.core_idea: Fearing death may be like a lost child

items.plain: Those who dream of feasts wake to grief; those who dream of grief wake to go hunting. While dreaming, they don't know it's a dream; only waking shows it. A Great Awakening will reveal this life as a great dream.
items.core_idea: Life itself may be a great dream

items.plain: Suppose you and I argue. If you win, are you necessarily right and I wrong, or the other way round? Or are we each partly right and partly wrong, or both entirely right or entirely wrong?
items.core_idea: Winning an argument doesn't prove you right

items.plain: Chuang Tzu dreamed he was a butterfly, fluttering about, unaware of being a man. He woke as himself, and now can't tell if he was a man dreaming he was a butterfly, or is a butterfly dreaming he's a man.
items.core_idea: Am I a man or a dreaming butterfly?

items.plain: My life is limited, but knowledge has no limit. Using what is limited to chase what is limitless is ruinous, and those who try it lose themselves.
items.core_idea: Chasing limitless knowledge with a limited life ruins you
